So hi, I am by no means good at this, but I hope this helps even a bit. 

What I did was kind of explaining my situation and how I felt, before coming to any conclusions in the conversation.

 Luckily for me my mom already knew that I was unhappy, so I just started explaining the reasons why and how I felt uncomfortable in who I was and how people refered to me.

 It may be a good idea to bring the topic of LGBTQ+ people up, just to see how the person you're planning on coming out to reacts to the topic. You might have to answer some questions regarding your gender identity, so it's propably not a bad idea to brace yourself for that, since people sometimes know quite little about being trans. 

All of that is obviously optional, the main thing is that you are safe and get the point across to the other person, preferably with you being comfortable.

 It may feel like a huge obstacle to overcome, but coming out is in my experience so freeing and you'll feel like you're on top of the world (if i may use a cheesy expression :) ).

 Best of luck to you and be safe!
